_comment: Pins for the repo-local .venv that scripts/setup-env.sh builds (never a host-wide tool): klayout-tools (klt) for the layout/ and sim/ flows, numpy for the behavioural DR-002 benches and scripts/cdr-loop-analysis.py. Append-only history: record later bumps as new entries in 'history', never edit an earlier one.
history: Issue #3: initial pin at klayout-tools main 267ea83 (merge of PR #3774), the commit whose docs/cli/sim.md the smoke request was written against.

Issue #42: bump to klayout-tools 0.8.0 from PyPI (tag v0.8.0, commit c572046be644). A PyPI install has no direct_url.json vcs_info, so scripts/setup-env.sh now verifies the installed version instead of the commit; klt_last_verified_commit records the tag commit for reference.

Issue #80: bump to klayout-tools 0.9.0 from PyPI (tag v0.9.0, commit 5dbbad05ff42), the version the batch fleet runner reports (runner_klt_version 0.9.0, re-read 2026-11-10); a client/runner skew made every batch unit error batch_runner_version_mismatch. Follows the fleet-tracking direction in 2AMLogic/2am#7038.

Issue #158: add bench_install numpy==2.3.4 from PyPI. The behavioural benches (sim/bench/link_r*.py) and scripts/cdr-loop-analysis.py declare numpy as their only third-party dependency (sim/README.md, DR-007), but nothing in the tree installed it, and `klt signoff --attest 9` runs the benches as cold_start checks in a sanitized environment (no .venv/bin on PATH, no VIRTUAL_ENV) whose python3 is the host interpreter -- so --regen and the benches worked only on hosts that happened to carry a compatible numpy. setup-env.sh now installs this pin into .venv (self-contained, no --system-site-packages) and run-bench.sh resolves .venv/bin/python3 by path, so the same pin serves every consumer. Verified on a numpy-free isolated interpreter: link_r13-offset exits 0 both after `source scripts/env.sh` and under a scrubbed environment, and a live item 9 attest reports 65/66 with zero numpy errors -- all five behavioural cold_starts pass; the one miss is a link-r8-sensitivity cold_start timeout on a loaded shared worker, tracked separately (issue #170).
